what: The first time the update chain was ever run. Eighteen releases had been published and no install had received one.

run_against_the_live_release.how: check_latest against the real GitHub API from a simulated 0.2.3 install, then download_and_verify against the real 75 MB asset.
run_against_the_live_release.sha256: matched the digest GitHub records on the asset
run_against_the_live_release.verdict: check -> offer -> download -> verify works end to end. That path had a `pragma: no cover - exercised in the field, not in tests` on it and had never been exercised in the field either.

found_by_running_it.defect: The handoff interpolated both paths into PowerShell single-quoted strings, so an apostrophe in the Windows account name ended the string early: 'C:\Users\O'Brien\...' parses as the literal C:\Users\O followed by bare tokens.
found_by_running_it.reach: Every user named O'Brien, D'Angelo, O'Connor. Both paths carry the account name - the installer sits under %LOCALAPPDATA% and the relaunch target is sys.executable under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs - so the update did nothing, with nothing in the app to say why.
found_by_running_it.fix: PowerShell's one escape: a literal quote is written twice.
found_by_running_it.not_an_injection: Windows account names disallow ; and ", so this was a breakage rather than a way in. It was fixed as a quoting bug, not a vulnerability.

found_by_running_it.defect: The release asset name was accepted on its ends alone - starts with OpenKnowledge-Setup-, ends with .exe - and then used as a filename to write into the state directory and execute.
found_by_running_it.why_it_matters: That name is the only remote data this product turns into a running program. A name containing a separator would have written outside the directory the state dir owns.
found_by_running_it.fix: Matched whole against OpenKnowledge-Setup-[0-9A-Za-z._-]+.exe. A release whose asset does not match simply offers no update, which is the existing behaviour for a release with no verifiable installer.

what_ci_now_proves: A windows-upgrade job installs the previous published release, writes a document and an .env into the per-user state directory, runs the new installer over it with the flags the app hands it, and asserts the installed --version moved and both files survived. It found the defect above on its first run, and its second green run is the first evidence in this project's history that an install can receive a build.
still_unproven: The final hop - the app quitting, the detached PowerShell running while its parent dies, and the relaunch - needs a real desktop session. CI installs over an idle install, which is the same situation the app arranges by quitting first, but it is not the same as watching it happen from inside the app.
pinned_by: tests/test_update.py: the apostrophe case and the asset-name case, both checked to fail against the previous code.

the_defect_the_new_job_found.symptom: An install does not receive a new build. The installer exits 0, replaces every file, and the app goes on reporting the version it just replaced.
the_defect_the_new_job_found.cause: PyInstaller bundles the package's .dist-info so the frozen app can read its own version, and the directory name carries that version. Inno replaces files; it never removes ones the new build no longer has. After a 0.2.18 -> 0.2.19 upgrade the install held BOTH openknowledge-0.2.18.dist-info and openknowledge-0.2.19.dist-info, and importlib.metadata answered with whichever it found first.
the_defect_the_new_job_found.measured_before: every file replaced, installer exit 0, installed --version still 'openknowledge 0.2.18'
the_defect_the_new_job_found.why_it_hid_for_eighteen_releases: v0.2.8 fixed the opposite failure - no metadata at all, so the version fell back to 0.0.0 and every comparison was nonsense. With metadata present the number looked plausible, so nothing downstream complained; the updater simply compared each new release against a version that never moved and offered the same update for ever. This is the whole of 'I still don't see the update button after several releases'.
the_defect_the_new_job_found.fix: [InstallDelete] clears {app}\_internal\openknowledge-*.dist-info before the files land. Scoped to the metadata rather than all of _internal: this is the defect that is measured, and wiping the runtime would fail badly for anyone who runs the installer with the app still open.
the_defect_the_new_job_found.still_true: Anything else a build stops shipping still lingers on an upgrade. Recorded in ROADMAP with what fixing it properly would take - the installer stopping the app first.

the_job_hanging.what: In the release pipeline the same job that had passed in 19 seconds ran 32 minutes without finishing, and an in-progress job serves no logs, so the hang could not be read.
changed: timeout-minutes: 15, so a step waiting on something nobody can answer fails in a quarter of an hour rather than six hours
Inno's logs upload with if: always(), because a killed step never reaches the Write-Host that dumped them
$ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue' before the 75 MB download - Invoke-WebRequest renders a progress bar with no console to render it to, which on a large file dominates the transfer
the_job_hanging.outcome: The release ran green and published, so the job passed inside it.
the_job_hanging.honestly: The progress-bar overhead is the strongly indicated cause and the only change that could plausibly unstick a download; it is not proven, because the hung run's logs never existed to read. If it recurs, the always-upload artifact is now there to say so.
